chapter: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
title: Dud Bascomb's son on Fender bass
summary: Bascomb's son is a fine New York bassist with a Fender; like father, like son.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Well, I just wanted to mention that, which I don't know whether we had on here, was that Dud Bascomb's son now is one of the greatest bass players, one of the finest bass players in New York City now.
Oh, yes, I have worked with him.
Yeah, I've worked with him and he's something else with that Fender bass, gee whiz.
He sure is. He's really out of sight.
He's really got it under his fingers.
Because he can play it as fast as a guitar player.
Yeah, he's a fantastic kid. He plays so beautifully on that Fender bass and he's an excellent musician.
A very mild-mannered gentleman, a credit to the whole music business.
But, you see, like father, like son.
That's where that is. You see, he was raised that way.
And his surroundings that he came up in as a kid made him like that, you see.
